strengths_deep_dive: The Palestine Children's Relief Fund maintains high program spending efficiency. In FY2024, it achieved an <cite id="4">87.2% program expense ratio</cite>, beating the 75% sector benchmark. This ensures that the majority of contributions fund direct pediatric medical care, specialized surgeries, and urgent relief. The organization raised <cite id="3">$94,873,840 in total revenue in FY2024</cite> while spending only <cite id="1">$0.02 per $1 raised</cite>. Operations in 2024 provided direct medical interventions, including <cite id="7">1,505 surgeries via global medical missions</cite> and emergency distributions of <cite id="7">82,696 food parcels in Gaza</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: The Palestine Children's Relief Fund provides direct medical care and humanitarian relief to children in the Middle East regardless of religion or political affiliation. Founded in 1991, the organization delivers specialized surgical operations, medical missions, and emergency relief across Gaza, the West Bank, Lebanon, Jordan, and Egypt. In FY2024, the charity managed <cite id="3">$94,873,840 in total revenue</cite>, reflecting massive growth in donor support during ongoing humanitarian crises in the region. <cite id="4">Financial filings from FY2024 show an 87.2% program expense ratio</cite>, directing the vast majority of expenditure toward direct healthcare and emergency aid. The organization maintains a <cite id="2">dedicated Zakat Fund</cite> that supports zakat-eligible beneficiaries. In FY2024, the charity conducted <cite id="7">1,324 emergency surgeries in Gaza</cite> and <cite id="7">1,505 surgeries via global medical missions</cite>. While operational delivery is strong, the organization holds <cite id="1">40.9 months of working capital reserves</cite>, which is unusually high for a zakat-collecting entity.
